correctness.rationale: The lower bound follows from one chosen word per length-(n-1) prefix class: two words of the same prefix have identical positive-step predecessor sets. Two explicit hexadecimal selector integers define complete attaining codebooks, one per prefix class. Exhaustive standard-library Python checks computed 128 and 512 nonempty, pairwise unique incoming-ball signatures using the exact suffix-prefix formula; a separate C++ reverse-BFS graph traversal independently reconstructed them. No evidence is extrapolated past the two stated parameter pairs.

evidence: Theorem 3.5: lower bound (d-1)d^(n-1). Theorems 3.6-3.7 construct minima when n>=2t. Theorem 3.9 constructs a potentially larger code for n=2t-1 and explicitly calls the optimum an open problem. Corollary 4.7 asserts equality only when 2t<=n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For (7,4) and (9,5), 2t=n+1, so the optimal-construction theorem does not apply; the lower bound alone cannot assert its attainment. The new explicit certificates close that logical gap at these two parameter pairs.

originality.rationale: The full relevant primary preprint arXiv:1412.5842 explicitly confines its minimum-size constructions to n>=2t and leaves n=2t-1 unresolved. The present size-64 and size-256 certificates resolve two distinct later boundary instances not implied by its general lower bound. The earlier own finite (n,t)=(5,3) result is excluded from the new claim. Broad semantic and parameter searches in published records and literature did not reveal a dominating statement. Unindexed priority remains a real residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed subsequent work, theses, or independent unpublished computations could already contain one or both finite optima.
The undirected comparison source was inspected by abstract rather than full text; it has a different graph model.
Scientific review and code replay are same-model, not independent peer review.

value.rationale: The exact optimum at the sharp identifiability boundary n=2t-1 is identified as open in the 2014 primary paper. These first two next higher binary radii after the previously resolved (5,3) case provide meaningful exact 128- and 512-vertex sensor-placement solutions, attaining a bound that was not known sharp at this boundary, and supply independently checkable finite witnesses. The value is the motivated cutoff, not generalization beyond the two proved parameters.
